land.text: the Satara State of 7,924 km2 (1848): the Satara district and parts of Pune, Sangli, Solapur and Bijapur districts

predecessors.note: The Satara State page: "created after the fall of the Maratha Confederacy in 1818 following the Third Anglo-Maratha War"; Pratap Singh "installed on the throne by the British after they defeated Peshwa Bajirao II in 1818". The Chhatrapati had held court at Satara since Shahu "ascended the throne at Satara on 12th January, 1708" (Shahu I page), inside the Maratha Empire shape; the Satara State page lists the Chhatrapatis from Shivaji I in its rulers table.

land.text: the Satara State of 7,924 km2 (1848): the Satara district and parts of Pune, Sangli, Solapur and Bijapur districts

successors.note: "The Company refused to accept Shahaji's adopted son as his successor" and the territory was "absorbed" into British dominion; the Doctrine of lapse page: "the Company took over the princely states of Satara (1848)".

capitals.name: Satara
capitals.note: Infobox Capital: Satara. Pratap Singh was allowed the throne but lived in exile in Varanasi (Pratap Singh page, undated).

rulers.name: Pratap Singh
rulers.note: Infobox reign 3 June 1818 to 5 September 1839, coronation 9 April 1818 (the body text gives 3 June 1818 for the crowning); the Satara State page says "deposed in 1838" and has the rulers list 1808-1839; the Pratap Singh page says dethroned and stripped of his powers in 1839.

rulers.name: Shahji III (Appa Saheb)
rulers.note: The last ruler; the infobox gives 1839-1849, the rulers list 1839-1848; "died without a natural heir in 1848".

correction.text: the Satara State of 7,924 km2 (1848): the Satara district and parts of Pune, Sangli, Solapur and Bijapur districts

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives 7,924 km2 (1848) and 11,144 km2 (1901, the later district) and says the state "comprised the modern day Satara district, and parts of the Pune district", with parts of the Sangli, Solapur and Bijapur districts; a 50 km circle about Satara (about 7,900 km2, ratio 1.0) stands in for all years. The state was scattered in fact; the pages give no boundary. Lies inside the Maratha Empire shape until 1818.

region.text: the Satara State of 7,924 km2 (1848): the Satara district and parts of Pune, Sangli, Solapur and Bijapur districts

ledger.note: 1818: Satara State is created for Pratap Singh after the fall of the Peshwa. "created after the fall of the Maratha Confederacy in 1818 following the Third Anglo-Maratha War"; Pratap Singh was "installed on the throne by the British after they defeated Peshwa Bajirao II in 1818" (Pratap Singh page: coronation 9 April 1818 and reign from 3 June 1818, which conflict; the page gives no month with certainty). The extent is the page's districts as a circle (my reading); Shahu I page: the Chhatrapati had ruled from Satara since 12 January 1708.

region.text: the Satara State of 7,924 km2 (1848): the Satara district and parts of Pune, Sangli, Solapur and Bijapur districts

ledger.note: 1848: the East India Company annexes Satara under the doctrine of lapse. "the Company took over the princely states of Satara (1848)" (also in the table); the Satara State page: Shahaji "died without a natural heir in 1848", the Company "refused to accept Shahaji's adopted son as his successor", and the territory was "absorbed"; but its introduction and infobox give 1849. The land annexed is the state (not described on the Doctrine of lapse page).

certainty.note: The pages give an area and districts but no boundary; the shape is a circle of the 1848 area.

sources.title: Satara State
sources.note: Princely state created 1818 after the fall of the Maratha Confederacy; Pratap Singh installed by the British; deposed 1838/1839; Shahaji died without heir 1848; area 7,924 km2 (1848); Satara district and parts of Pune, Sangli, Solapur and Bijapur districts.

sources.title: Pratap Singh of Satara
sources.note: Reign 3 June 1818 to 5 September 1839 (infobox), coronation 9 April 1818; dethroned in 1839; exiled to Varanasi, died 1847; succeeded by his brother Appa Saheb; silent on territory.

sources.title: Doctrine of lapse
sources.note: Lists Satara among the states the Company took over (1848); Jhansi 1853, Nagpur 1854 (text) or 1853 (table), Jaitpur and Sambalpur 1849, Udaipur (Chhattisgarh) 1852.

sources.title: Shahu I
sources.note: Shahu ascended the throne at Satara on 12 January 1708 and held his court there until 15 December 1749; Rangmahal Palace from 1721; background for the later Satara State.

notes: Four pages opened (Satara State, Pratap Singh of Satara, Doctrine of lapse, Shahu I). Conflicts: annexation 1848 (text, table, death of Shahaji) against 1849 (Satara State introduction and infobox); Pratap Singh deposed in 1838 (Satara State) against 1839 (his own page, rulers list); coronation 9 April 1818 against reign from 3 June 1818. The dossier ends in 1848. The Maratha Chhatrapati kingdom of Satara before 1818 lies inside the maratha-empire shape (which ends in 1818); the Treaty of Warna, the 1731 date and the Rangmahal move of 1721 are for the maratha-empire and kolhapur-state dossiers (the Shahu I page says Warana made Kolhapur "a firmly subordinate sector of Satara Chhatrapati's realm", undated). The british-empire dossier should record the vassal_start for satara-state from 1818 to 1848. The Doctrine of lapse page also dates other annexations: Jhansi 1853, Nagpur 1854 in the text and 1853 in the table (kingdom-of-nagpur ends in 1853), Jaitpur and Sambalpur 1849, Udaipur (Chhattisgarh) 1852; Jhansi, Sambalpur and Jaitpur have no dossier.
